title: Accept-Language parser fails on wildcard '*' in 0.22
description: The `Accept-Language` header parser in http4s 0.22+ rejects the wildcard token `*;q=0.5` even though it is a valid production per RFC 9110 §12.5.4. The example value `fr-CH, fr;q=0.9, en;q=0.8, de;q=0.7, *;q=0.5` (taken verbatim from MDN) parses successfully on http4s 0.21.24 but fails on 0.22.2 and later, with the parser reporting `Error(0,NonEmptyList(InRange(0,A,Z), InRange(0,a,z)))` — i.e. it expects an alphabetic language tag where the wildcard `*` appears. This breaks content-negotiation for any REST client that sends a valid `Accept-Language` header containing a wildcard catch-all entry, and causes server-side handlers that call `Accept-Language.parse(...)` to receive `Left(ParseFailure(...))` instead of `Right(...)`. The fix (PR #5070) updates the parser grammar to accept `*` as a valid `language-range` production, mirroring RFC 9110 §12.5.4.
